passages.text: A prayer of Moses the man of God.
passages.sermon: Moses was a man of God.\r\nThis is his prayer.

passages.text: Lord, You have been our dwelling place through all generations.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a man of God.
Moses prayed to the Lord.
Lord, You are our dwelling place.
You have been our home for us.
You have done this through all generations.
passages.original: תְּפִלָּה֮ לְמֹשֶׁ֪ה אִֽישׁ־ הָאֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים אֲ‍ֽדֹנָ֗י מָע֣וֹן אַ֭תָּה הָיִ֥יתָ לָּ֗נוּ בְּדֹ֣ר וָדֹֽר׃

passages.text: Before the mountains were born or You brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting You are God.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a man of God.
Moses prayed to the Lord.
God existed before the mountains were born.
God created the earth and the world.
God has no beginning or end.
God is everlasting.
God is always God.
passages.original: בְּטֶ֤רֶם׀ הָ֘רִ֤ים יֻלָּ֗דוּ וַתְּח֣וֹלֵֽל אֶ֣רֶץ וְתֵבֵ֑ל וּֽמֵעוֹלָ֥ם עַד־ ע֝וֹלָ֗ם אַתָּ֥ה אֵֽל׃

passages.text: You return man to dust, saying, “Return, O sons of mortals.”
passages.sermon:
God is eternal.
God existed before the world began.
God created everything.
God has power over all people.
God returns people to dust.
God says, “Return, O sons of mortals.”
People are mortal.
God commands people to return to their origin.
passages.original: תָּשֵׁ֣ב אֱ֭נוֹשׁ עַד־ דַּכָּ֑א וַ֝תֹּ֗אמֶר שׁ֣וּבוּ בְנֵי־ אָדָֽם׃

passages.text: For in Your sight a thousand years are but a day that passes, or a watch of the night.
passages.sermon:
God is eternal.
God sees time differently than people.
A thousand years to God is like one day that has passed.
A thousand years to God is also like a short watch in the night.
Time is very brief to God.
passages.original: כִּ֤י אֶ֪לֶף שָׁנִ֡ים בְּֽעֵינֶ֗יךָ כְּי֣וֹם אֶ֭תְמוֹל כִּ֣י יַעֲבֹ֑ר וְאַשְׁמוּרָ֥ה בַלָּֽיְלָה׃

passages.text: You whisk them away in their sleep; they are like the new grass of the morning— in the morning it springs up new, but by evening it fades and withers.
passages.sermon:
God rules over human life.
God removes people from life as if in their sleep.
People are like new grass in the morning.
In the morning, the grass grows fresh and strong.
By evening, the grass dries up and withers away.
passages.original: זְ֭רַמְתָּם שֵׁנָ֣ה יִהְי֑וּ בַּ֝בֹּ֗קֶר כֶּחָצִ֥יר יַחֲלֹֽף׃ בַּ֭בֹּקֶר יָצִ֣יץ וְחָלָ֑ף לָ֝עֶ֗רֶב יְמוֹלֵ֥ל וְיָבֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: For we are consumed by Your anger and terrified by Your wrath.
passages.sermon:
God is angry.
God shows wrath.
We feel His anger.
His anger consumes us.
We see His wrath.
His wrath terrifies us.

passages.text: You have set our iniquities before You, our secret sins in the light of Your presence.
passages.sermon:
God sees everything.
\r\nGod knows our sins.
\r\nGod puts our sins in front of Him.
\r\nGod also knows our secret sins.
\r\nGod brings our hidden sins into His light.
\r\nNothing is hidden from God’s presence.
passages.original: שַׁתָּ עֲוֺנֹתֵ֣ינוּ לְנֶגְדֶּ֑ךָ עֲ֝לֻמֵ֗נוּ לִמְא֥וֹר פָּנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: For all our days decline in Your fury; we finish our years with a sigh.
passages.sermon:
God is angry with us.
His anger causes our days to fade away.
All our days pass under His fury.
We end our years with a sigh.
Our lives come to a weary end.
passages.original: כִּ֣י כָל־ יָ֭מֵינוּ פָּנ֣וּ בְעֶבְרָתֶ֑ךָ כִּלִּ֖ינוּ שָׁנֵ֣ינוּ כְמוֹ־ הֶֽגֶה׃

passages.text: The length of our days is seventy years— or eighty if we are strong— yet their pride is but labor and sorrow, for they quickly pass, and we fly away.
passages.sermon:
God gives most people about seventy years of life.
Some people live eighty years if they are strong.
Even the best years bring only hard work and trouble.
Our years end quickly.
We soon pass away.
passages.original: יְמֵֽי־ שְׁנוֹתֵ֨ינוּ בָהֶ֥ם שִׁבְעִ֪ים שָׁנָ֡ה וְאִ֤ם בִּגְבוּרֹ֨ת׀ שְׁמ֘וֹנִ֤ים שָׁנָ֗ה וְ֭רָהְבָּם עָמָ֣ל וָאָ֑וֶן כִּי־ גָ֥ז חִ֝֗ישׁ וַנָּעֻֽפָה׃

passages.text: Who knows the power of Your anger? Your wrath matches the fear You are due.
passages.sermon:
God is powerful.
God becomes angry.
No one fully understands the strength of God's anger.
God deserves great fear and respect.
God's wrath is as great as the fear He deserves.
passages.original: מִֽי־ י֭וֹדֵעַ עֹ֣ז אַפֶּ֑ךָ וּ֝כְיִרְאָתְךָ֗ עֶבְרָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: So teach us to number our days, that we may present a heart of wisdom.
passages.sermon:
God, You are eternal and wise.
We are people with short lives.
Our days are few and pass quickly.
Teach us to count each day carefully.
Help us understand the value of our time.
When we learn this, we gain wisdom in our hearts.
passages.original: לִמְנ֣וֹת יָ֭מֵינוּ כֵּ֣ן הוֹדַ֑ע וְ֝נָבִ֗א לְבַ֣ב חָכְמָֽה׃

passages.text: Return, O LORD! How long will it be? Have compassion on Your servants.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses the LORD.
The LORD is God.
The speaker asks the LORD to return.
The speaker asks, "How long will it be?"
The speaker asks the LORD to have compassion.
The speaker asks the LORD to show compassion to His servants.
passages.original: שׁוּבָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה עַד־ מָתָ֑י וְ֝הִנָּחֵ֗ם עַל־ עֲבָדֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Satisfy us in the morning with Your loving devotion, that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.
passages.sermon:
God, You are loving and devoted.
Satisfy us in the morning with Your love.
Then we will sing for joy.
Then we will be glad all our days.
passages.original: שַׂבְּעֵ֣נוּ בַבֹּ֣קֶר חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ וּֽנְרַנְּנָ֥ה וְ֝נִשְׂמְחָ֗ה בְּכָל־ יָמֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil.
passages.sermon:
God, You have afflicted us for many days.
We have seen evil for many years.
Make us glad for the same number of days.
Give us joy for as many years as we have suffered.
passages.original: שַׂ֭מְּחֵנוּ כִּימ֣וֹת עִנִּיתָ֑נוּ שְׁ֝נ֗וֹת רָאִ֥ינוּ רָעָֽה׃

passages.text: May Your work be shown to Your servants, and Your splendor to their children.
passages.sermon:
God, You have servants.
\r\nShow Your work to Your servants.
\r\nYou have children of Your servants.
\r\nShow Your splendor to their children.
passages.original: יֵרָאֶ֣ה אֶל־ עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ פָעֳלֶ֑ךָ וַ֝הֲדָרְךָ֗ עַל־ בְּנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: May the favor of the Lord our God rest upon us; establish for us the work of our hands— yes, establish the work of our hands!
passages.sermon:
The Lord is our God.
We ask for His favor.
We want His favor to rest on us.
We ask God to make our work strong.
We ask God to make the work of our hands last.
We ask Him again to make the work of our hands firm.
passages.original: וִיהִ֤י׀ נֹ֤עַם אֲדֹנָ֥י אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ עָ֫לֵ֥ינוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָ֭דֵינוּ כּוֹנְנָ֥ה עָלֵ֑ינוּ וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָ֝דֵ֗ינוּ כּוֹנְנֵֽהוּ׃
